plan.contextChunk: This figure is a heavily labeled diagram of a hyperbola opening left and right, centered at the origin of a coordinate system with arrowhead-tipped axes marked x at the right and y at the top. Two dark blue branches sweep away from the horizontal axis, one on each side. A pair of orange dashed lines cross at the center and run diagonally to the corners of the drawing, each tagged by a leader arrow reading "Asymptote" at the lower left and lower right. A teal dashed rectangle is centered on the origin, its vertical sides passing through the turning points of the two branches and its horizontal sides passing through two points on the vertical axis, with its corners sitting on the orange diagonals. A short red segment along the horizontal axis joins the two turning points and is labeled "Transverse axis" by an arrow pointing down onto it; a light blue segment along the vertical axis joins the top and bottom of the rectangle and is labeled "Conjugate axis." Dark blue dots at the ends of the red segment are each labeled "Vertex," light blue dots at the ends of the vertical segment are each labeled "Co-vertex," teal dots farther out along the horizontal axis are each labeled "Focus," and an orange marker at the crossing point is labeled "Center." Assembling every named element on one curve shows how the rectangle and its extended diagonals govern the directions the branches approach.

demo_steps.title: Identify the construction
demo_steps.narration: The center is at the origin, the red transverse axis connects the two vertices, and the light blue conjugate axis sets the rectangle height. The dashed rectangle’s diagonals are the asymptotes.

demo_steps.title: Change the transverse axis
demo_steps.narration: Lengthening the transverse axis pushes the vertices outward from the center. The branches begin farther from the origin, and the guide rectangle widens.

demo_steps.title: Change the conjugate axis
demo_steps.narration: Increasing the conjugate axis height makes the guide rectangle taller. The asymptotes become steeper, so the hyperbola branches open in a different direction pattern.

demo_steps.title: View the final curve
demo_steps.narration: Hide the construction guides and the blue branches remain. The rectangle and asymptotes are not extra parts of the curve; they explain why the curve has this shape.

interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: Use a centered coordinate plane with a horizontal hyperbola opening left and right. Let the transverse length slider define vertices at x = ±a and the conjugate length slider define co-vertices at y = ±b, with a = transverseLength/2 and b = conjugateLength/2. Draw the hyperbola as x^2/a^2 - y^2/b^2 = 1, with foci at x = ±sqrt(a^2 + b^2). Use dark blue for branches and vertex dots, red for the transverse axis, light blue for the conjugate axis and co-vertex dots, teal for foci and the dashed guide rectangle, and orange for the center point and dashed asymptotes y = ±(b/a)x. Keep labels in a textbook-style serif font with leader arrows, but allow the guide rectangle, asymptotes, and their labels to disappear when guides are hidden.

authoredContext:
As with the ellipse, every hyperbola has two axes of symmetry. The transverse axis is a line segment that passes through the center of the hyperbola and has vertices as its endpoints. The foci lie on the line that contains the transverse axis. The conjugate axis is perpendicular to the transverse axis and has the co-vertices as its endpoints. The center of a hyperbola is the midpoint of both the transverse and conjugate axes, where they intersect. Every hyperbola also has two asymptotes that pass through its center. As a hyperbola recedes from the center, its branches approach these asymptotes. The central rectangle of the hyperbola is centered at the origin with sides that pass through each vertex and co-vertex; it is a useful tool for graphing the hyperbola and its asymptotes. To sketch the asymptotes of the hyperbola, simply sketch and extend the diagonals of the central rectangle. See the figure.

Key features of the hyperbola

This diagram illustrates the various components of a hyperbola centered at the origin, including the vertices, co-vertices, foci, transverse axis, conjugate axis, asymptotes, and the rectangular box used to construct the asymptotes.

In this section, we will limit our discussion to hyperbolas that are positioned vertically or horizontally in the coordinate plane; the axes will either lie on or be parallel to the x- and y-axes. We will consider two cases: those that are centered at the origin, and those that are centered at a point other than the origin.

discrepancies: Several annotations are more crowded than in the source, especially the upper-left 'Conjugate axis' and 'Co-vertex' labels and their leaders, which visually collide more than the clean textbook layout.
The 'y' label is placed very close to or overlapping the top arrowhead, whereas the source keeps it clearly above the axis tip.

Some leader arrows point less precisely than the source, such as the conjugate-axis leader terminating in the interior of the guide rectangle rather than cleanly identifying the vertical blue conjugate axis.
The generated default includes a large control panel beside the diagram, so the overall composition is less like a standalone drop-in textbook figure even though the main SVG content is faithful.
evaluation.notes: The hyperbola, axes, vertices, foci, co-vertices, guide rectangle, and asymptotes are all accurately represented, but label placement is somewhat crowded compared with the source.
action_items: Reposition the upper-left 'Conjugate axis' and 'Co-vertex' annotations so their text and leader lines do not visually interfere.
Move the 'y' label higher or slightly offset it so it does not overlap the top arrowhead.
Adjust leader endpoints to land more exactly on the intended primitives, especially the conjugate axis and asymptotes.
For a closer static match, reduce the visual footprint of the right-side UI or allow a default static-only view.
